title: Crossing situation: who gives way? COLREG Rule 15 explained
description: COLREG Rule 15 in 3D: two power-driven vessels crossing with risk of collision. Who is the give-way vessel, what action is expected, and the common mistake of small alterations.

source.title: Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 (COLREG)

script: Two power-driven vessels are crossing, and there is risk of collision. Who gives way? You are heading north. Another vessel is crossing from your starboard side, and her compass bearing is not changing. Under Rule 15, you are the give-way vessel. The usual action: alter course to starboard, early and substantially, and pass astern of her. The give-way vessel takes early and substantial action to keep well clear, and avoids crossing ahead of the other. The stand-on vessel keeps her course and speed, but she must keep watching. The common mistake is a series of small alterations. Rule 8 requires an action large enough to be readily apparent to the other vessel, visually or by radar. Remember: if she is on your starboard side, you give way. Follow HeyMariner for practical maritime knowledge.
